sections.html: Wertheimeria maculata belongs to the strangest thorny catfishes. Adults are about 30 cm long and look spectacular: on a black background the species has large, cream-colored spots.

South America: Jequitinhonha River basin, Brazil. Type locality: Rio Jequitinhonha [Brazil].

Wertheimeria maculata is endemic to the Jequitinhonha and Pardo rivers in eastern Brazil.

Specimens were captured mostly during the rainy season, in the main channel and larger tributaries only, specifically in deep pools at running or backwater sites, and most efficiently by artisanal fishermen traps made with bamboo and lianas.

Within its restricted range, W. maculata faces strong human habitat disturbances such as siltation, habitat fragmentation, pollution, and introduced species.
They have no special demands on water, but it goes without saying that they should be kept in aquariums as large as possible with well maintained water.
Wertheimeria maculata do not have special demands on food, but they should be fed with high quality food (mussel meat is ideal, but any commercially available ornamental fish food is accepted).
The diet is diversified and includes mainly allochthonous resources, especially fruits and terrestrial insects derived from the riparian vegetation.

Whoever acquires this species should keep it for himself if possible. Young animals are compatible with each other. The animals are hiding-loving and mainly nocturnal and are easily disturbed by other species. One hardly gets to see them then.

Partial spawning is suggested for the species based on the capture of individuals in advanced maturation and totally spawned in distinct temporal periods. It is being bred successfully in Brazil by the Brazilian exporter Hudson Crizanto Gonçalves.

The genus Wertheimeria was established for the species at its first description in 1877 and it remains the only member to this day. Within the spiny catfishes (Doradidae) a separate subfamily Wertheimerinae was established for the species and two others (Franciscodoras marmoratus and Kalyptodoras bahiensis).

Aquarium care: Not a lot is known about the husbandry of this large Dorad.

Colouration: Its unique life colour pattern consists of reddish to olivaceous ground colour with large whitish vermiculations in small specimens, and sparse dots in larger ones (Vono et al.).

Wertheimeria maculata is the only species in the genus Wertheimeria from the catfish family Doradidae. This fish has been placed as the sister taxon to all other doradids.

Etymology: The genus name Wertheimeria honours Mr. Wertheimer, who collected the holotype, either Louis Wertheimer of the Thayer Expedition to Brazil (1865–1866), or Achilles Wertheimer, who died on the expedition due to a snakebite. The specific name maculata is Latin for spotted, referring to large, oval, blue-gray spots on upper body, top of head, and pectoral and dorsal fins.

Remarks: All Doradidae examined have retrorse thorns on their midlateral scutes, except for Wertheimeria, which lacks thorns. Wertheimeria maculata generally has three scutes on the anterior portion of the body, and the remaining portion of the lateral line is tubule shaped and unossified, similar to those found in auchenipterids.
